mainTopic: Customs of אנשי יריחו: קצירה, גמזיות של הקדש, פורצין פרצות with the מוקצה debate, and פאה from vegetables
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's look at the customs of אנשי יריחו from the משנה. First, the גמרא removes קצירה from the list of things the חכמים 'did not protest,' because רבי יהודה holds harvesting had their full approval and the count would otherwise be four instead of three. Next, it explains the dispute over גמזיות של הקדש: the branches are later growth with no מעילה, but the חכמים hold there is still an איסור. On פורצין פרצות, עולא quoting ריש לקיש places the dispute on dates resting on the high branches, where the חכמים fear someone will climb and pick. רבא challenges this, arguing that the fallen dates are מוקצה. עולא answers that whatever is ready for ravens is ready for people, because a person's mind is always on food fit for him. רבין then reports a different version of ריש לקיש, in which the dispute is about the low branches. Finally, the גמרא asks how אנשי יריחו could give פאה from vegetables. רב answers that the case is turnip heads, and the dispute is whether storage by means of something else (per רש״י, the leaves kept with the bulbs) counts as storage. Two ברייתות about giving פאה from turnips, cabbage, and leeks close the amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says harvesting had the Sages' full approval
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the משנה's wording 'they protested / they did not protest' as the language of רבי יהודה. Yet רבי יהודה himself says harvesting was done ברצון חכמים, which means full approval, not mere silence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who have you heard use the wording 'they protested' and 'they did not protest'? רבי יהודה. Yet he teaches: they harvest with the Sages' approval!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The משנה's style matches רבי יהודה, but רבי יהודה says harvesting before the עומר was fully approved, so it does not belong among things the Sages merely 'did not protest.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Did not protest' means the Sages disliked the practice but stayed quiet. 'ברצון חכמים' means they actually agreed with it. If רבי יהודה holds harvesting was approved, listing it among the 'did not protest' items makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not protest (tolerated it without approving)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Did not protest' is NOT the same as 'approved.' The whole question depends on the difference between tolerating something and agreeing to it.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says
'they protested' and 'they did not protest'? Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר uses different wording: 'with the will' and 'against the will' of the Sages.

phrases.english: And yet he teaches: they harvest with the will of the Sages!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of the ברייתא's disagreement between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about the practices of אנשי יריחו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's placement of קצירה among the practices the Sages 'did not protest.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The author of the משנה is רבי יהודה, and he holds harvesting was fully approved. So it cannot also be counted among merely tolerated practices.

steps.title: The count would become four instead of three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second problem. If harvesting is counted separately, the 'did not protest' list has four items, but the משנה says three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, these are four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens the problem by counting the items. Grafting, bundling שמע, harvesting, and piling make four, but the משנה says only three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולטעמיך' means 'by your own logic.' The numbers do not work as the משנה is written. This sets up the fix in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, these are four!
phrases.notes: The list would be: grafting palms, bundling שמע, harvesting, and piling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a counting problem that confirms the difficulty from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's count of three practices that were not protested.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If קצירה is a separate item, the list has four entries, which contradicts the stated number three.

steps.title: Remove harvesting from the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves both problems by deleting קצירה from this list in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: remove 'harvesting' from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the text by taking harvesting out of the 'did not protest' list. This solves both the approval problem and the counting problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once קצירה is removed, three items remain, matching the משנה's number. It also fits רבי יהודה, because harvesting was fully approved and so never belonged among tolerated practices.

keyTerms.meaning: Remove from here (delete from the text)

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יהודה, harvesting before the עומר was fully approved by the חכמים. It is therefore deleted from the list of practices they merely did not protest.

phrases.english: Rather: remove harvesting from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulties raised in steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (deleting a word from the משנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Harvesting was listed as one of the practices the Sages did not protest.
steps.terutzMaskana: Harvesting is removed from that list. Three items remain, consistent with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: אנשי יריחו permitted consecrated carob and sycamore branches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next practice the Sages protested: אנשי יריחו permitted the use of consecrated branches. It also gives their reason: their ancestors consecrated only the trunks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they permit consecrated branches of carob and sycamore. They said: our fathers consecrated only the trunks, so we will permit consecrated branches of carob and sycamore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new item from the משנה. It states what אנשי יריחו did and their reasoning: the original הקדש covered only the trunks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carob and sycamore trees are valued for their trunks, which are used as building beams. אנשי יריחו argued that the branches were never part of the original consecration, so they could use them. The next steps explain the logic and why the Sages still objected.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property (belonging to the בית המקדש)

phrases.english: And they permit consecrated branches
of carob and of sycamore trees.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: אֲבוֹתֵינוּ לֹא הִקְדִּישׁוּ אֶלָּא קוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: They said: Our fathers consecrated only the trunks,
and we will permit consecrated branches
of carob and of sycamore trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new item in the list: the practices the Sages did protest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אנשי יריחו permitted the use of consecrated carob and sycamore branches, because only the trunks had been consecrated.

steps.title: Later growth carries no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the case concerns branches that grew after the consecration. אנשי יריחו follow the view that there is no מעילה on later growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with growth that came afterward, and they hold like the one who says: there is no מעילה on growth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies the exact case and the reasoning of אנשי יריחו. The branches grew only after the tree was consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that new growth on consecrated property is not covered by the law of מעילה (misuse of הקדש). אנשי יריחו followed that view, so they treated the new branches as permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition, with its penalty, against misusing consecrated property

phrases.english: And we are dealing with growth that came afterward,
and they hold like the one who says:
There is no misuse with regard to later growth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the case from step 4 and the legal basis of אנשי יריחו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: (Implicit) How could anyone permit consecrated property?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The branches are later growth, and there is no מעילה on later growth.

steps.title: No מעילה, but still an איסור
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree there is no מעילה on later growth, but they hold that using it is still forbidden. That is why they protested.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis hold: even though there is no מעילה, there is still a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the Sages objected. Even without מעילה, using the branches is still prohibited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is not about whether מעילה applies, since both sides agree it does not. The question is whether a lesser איסור remains. The חכמים say it does, so permitting the branches was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: At least there is a prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: On גמזיות, everyone agrees there is no מעילה on later growth. The חכמים protested only because a basic איסור still remains.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
Granted that there is no misuse,
in any case there is a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to step 5 and explains the Sages' protest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no מעילה on later growth of הקדש, but using it is still forbidden.

steps.title: The dispute concerns dates on the upper branches
steps.stepSummary: On the practice of making breaches in fences, עולא quoting ריש לקיש says the dispute is about fallen dates resting on the high branches (מכבדות). The חכמים make a גזירה that someone might climb up and pick, while אנשי יריחו do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they make breaches.' עולא said in the name of ריש לקיש: the dispute is about dates on the upper branches. The Rabbis hold we decree lest one climb and pick, and the men of Jericho hold we do not decree lest one climb and pick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next practice and gives עולא's explanation of exactly where the disagreement lies. The question is whether to forbid taking fallen dates from high branches out of fear that someone will climb and pick attached fruit on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנשי יריחו opened their fences so the poor could take fallen fruit on שבת and יום טוב. When fallen dates rest on the top branches, reaching them could lead a person to climb the tree and pick attached dates, which is forbidden. The חכמים decree against it, and אנשי יריחו do not.

keyTerms.meaning: They make breaches (open gaps in fences)
Lest he climb up and pick

phrases.english: And they make breaches.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
The dispute is about dates on the upper branches,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: גָּזְרִינַן שֶׁמָּא יַעֲלֶה וְיִתְלוֹשׁ,
phrases.english: for the Rabbis hold: we decree lest one climb and pick,
and the men of Jericho hold: we do not decree
lest one climb and pick.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפוֹרְצִין פְּרָצוֹת. אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next practice in the list and explains the dispute about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For dates on the upper branches, the חכמים forbid taking them because of a גזירה that one might climb and pick. אנשי יריחו permit it.

steps.title: Dates on the lower branches are permitted by all
steps.stepSummary: Dates that fell onto the low branches (בין הכיפין) are permitted according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding dates on the lower branches, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא finishes his statement by limiting the dispute. For low branches, no one forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates on low branches can be reached without climbing, so the fear behind the גזירה does not apply. This sharpens the point that the only disagreement concerns the high branches.

phrases.english: But regarding dates on the lower branches,
everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes עולא's statement by marking where there is no dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fallen dates on low branches are permitted by all.

steps.title: רבא: the fallen dates are מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges עולא. Dates that fell on שבת were still attached to the tree at the start of שבת, so they should be מוקצה regardless of any climbing concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But they are מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks עולא's claim that the lower-branch dates are permitted by all. Since they fell on שבת itself, they were not ready for use when שבת began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that could not be used at בין השמשות (twilight before שבת) stays forbidden all of שבת. At that time these dates were attached and unusable, so they should be מוקצה. That would make them forbidden even on low branches.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside, forbidden to handle or use on שבת

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But they are set-aside!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא מוּקְצוֹת נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's ruling in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's statement that fallen dates (at least on low branches) are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The dates were attached and unusable at the start of שבת, so they are מוקצה and should be forbidden no matter where they landed.

steps.title: Possible defense: the dates were fit for ravens
steps.stepSummary: רבא anticipates an answer. The dates were not מוקצה because, even while attached, ravens could eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: since they are fit for ravens.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a possible defense so he can knock it down next. The suggestion is that the dates counted as 'ready' before שבת because birds could eat them off the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that if something was usable for anyone at בין השמשות, even birds, it is not מוקצה. Attached dates were available to ravens, so perhaps they were 'prepared.' This is only a setup, and the next steps reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבא's own view. It is a suggested answer that he raises only to reject it.

phrases.english: And if you say: since they are fit for ravens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible defense against the מוקצה challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Anticipated answer (raised in order to be rejected)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dates are מוקצה because they were attached at the start of שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps they are not מוקצה, since ravens could eat them. (This is rejected in steps 11 and 12.)

steps.title: Food ready for people is not ready for dogs
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה in which רבי יהודה rules that an animal that died on שבת may not be given to dogs. While it was alive at the start of שבת it was ready for people, but not for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, what is ready for a person is not considered ready for dogs, as we learned: רבי יהודה says, if it was not a carcass from ערב שבת, it is forbidden, because it is not from the prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets up a קל וחומר. He first proves from a משנה that being 'ready' for one user does not make something ready for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living animal at the start of שבת could be slaughtered and eaten, so it was 'ready' for humans. Yet רבי יהודה says that if it dies on שבת it may not be fed to dogs. Readiness for people does not carry over to dogs.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if even (opens a קל וחומר)
Prepared, ready for use on שבת

phrases.english: Now, if what is prepared for a person
is not considered prepared for dogs,
as we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה נְבֵילָה מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: If it was not a carcass on Shabbat eve, it is forbidden,
because it is not among the prepared.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא מוּכָן לְאָדָם לָא הָוֵי מוּכָן לִכְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the rejection of step 10 by establishing a premise from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Being 'ready' for one type of user does not make something ready for another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה in the משנה about a נבילה that died on שבת (שבת קנ״ו:).

steps.title: Food ready for ravens cannot be ready for people
steps.stepSummary: רבא completes the קל וחומר. If readiness for people does not extend to dogs, readiness for ravens surely does not extend to people. The 'ravens' defense fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is what is ready for ravens considered ready for a person?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes knocking down the suggested defense. The dates' availability to ravens cannot make them permitted for humans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Humans are the main users for whom food is prepared, yet even that readiness does not pass to dogs. Readiness for ravens is much weaker, so it certainly cannot pass to humans. The מוקצה challenge against עולא therefore stands for now.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's challenge stands for now. Fallen dates seem to be מוקצה, and 'fit for ravens' does not help, by a קל וחומר from רבי יהודה's ruling about a נבילה.

phrases.english: Is what is prepared for ravens considered prepared for a person?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קל וחומר begun in step 11 and rejects the defense of step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'fit for ravens' answer to the מוקצה challenge.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Readiness does not transfer between users. If it does not transfer from people to dogs, it surely does not transfer from ravens to people.

steps.title: Readiness moves up to people but not down to dogs
steps.stepSummary: עולא agrees that readiness for people does not extend to dogs. He argues that readiness for ravens does extend to people, because a person's mind is always on anything fit for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to רבא: Yes. Something ready for a person is not ready for dogs, because a person never takes his mind off anything fit for people. But something ready for ravens is ready for a person, because a person's mind is always on anything fit for people.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רבא's קל וחומר. He shows that the two cases point in opposite directions, so one cannot be learned from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was alive at the start of שבת was set aside in the owner's mind for people, so it was never 'ready' for dogs. Dates that ravens could eat are different. A person is always ready to take food that is fit for him, so his mind was already on the dates. The קל וחומר fails because human interest only pulls things toward people, never away from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared or ready for use on שבת (the opposite of מוקצה)
Removes it from his mind (sets it aside mentally)
His mind is on it (he intends to use it)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a contradiction. Readiness for people does not count for dogs, while readiness for ravens does count for people. The deciding question is always whether the person's own mind is on the item, and a person's mind is always on human food.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a basic principle of מוקצה: a person's state of mind about an item decides whether it is ready for use on שבת.

phrases.english: He (עולא) said to him (רבא): Yes,

phrases.aramaic: מוּכָן לְאָדָם — לָא הָוֵי מוּכָן לִכְלָבִים,
phrases.english: something ready for a person is not ready for dogs,
because anything that is fit for a person,
he does not remove it from his mind.
phrases.notes: He keeps it for human use, so it is not set aside for dogs.

phrases.english: Something ready for ravens is ready for a person,
since anything that is fit for a person,
his mind is on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's קל וחומר from step 12 by showing the comparison does not work.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (the two cases run in opposite directions)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If readiness for people does not extend to dogs, then readiness for ravens surely does not extend to people.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person's mind is always on food fit for him. So readiness for ravens does extend to people, but readiness for people does not extend to dogs.

steps.title: רבין's different version of ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that ריש לקיש placed the dispute on dates that fell onto the low branches. Dates on the high branches are forbidden by everyone because of a decree against climbing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: The dispute is about dates on the low branches. The חכמים hold that what is ready for ravens is not ready for people. The people of יריחו hold that what is ready for ravens is ready for people. But dates on the high branches are forbidden according to everyone, because we make a decree in case a person climbs up and picks them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of ריש לקיש's teaching, reported by רבין. It differs from עולא's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עולא's version, the low-branch dates were permitted by everyone. In רבין's version, the low-branch dates are exactly where the dispute is: the חכמים forbid them and the people of יריחו permit them. In רבין's version, the high-branch dates are forbidden by everyone because of the climbing decree.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל with a teaching)
In case he climbs and picks (detaching from a tree on שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two versions apart. For עולא, the low branches are permitted by everyone. For רבין, the low branches are where the dispute is, and the high branches are forbidden by everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of ריש לקיש. In רבין's version, the argument between the חכמים and the people of יריחו is really about whether something ready for ravens counts as ready for people.

phrases.english: When רבין came,
he said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש:
The dispute is about dates on the low branches,
because the חכמים hold:

phrases.aramaic: מוּכָן לְעוֹרְבִים — לָא הָוֵי מוּכָן לְאָדָם,
phrases.english: what is ready for ravens is not ready for a person,
and the people of יריחו hold:
what is ready for ravens is ready for a person,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּשֶׁל מַכְבֵּדוֹת — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר,
phrases.english: but dates on the high branches are forbidden according to everyone,
since we decree in case he climbs and picks.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing version of ריש לקיש's teaching, which places the dispute on the low-branch dates that עולא's version permitted for everyone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is about low-branch dates and turns on whether readiness for ravens counts as readiness for people. High-branch dates are forbidden by everyone because of the climbing decree.

steps.title: Quoting the next custom of אנשי יריחו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה: the people of יריחו gave פאה from vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And they would give פאה from vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next custom of the people of יריחו from the משנה. This line is setting up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פאה is the corner of the field that is left for the poor. The people of יריחו left פאה even from vegetable fields. The גמרא is about to ask why they did this.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor

phrases.english: "And they would give פאה from vegetables."
phrases.notes: A quotation from the משנה listing the customs of the people of יריחו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the dates discussion and moves to a new custom from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of יריחו gave פאה from vegetables.

steps.title: Challenge from the general rule of פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the people of יריחו do not accept the משנה that lists five conditions for an obligation of פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't the people of יריחו accept what we learned in a משנה? A general rule was stated about פאה: anything that is food, is guarded, grows from the ground, is harvested all at once, and is brought in for storage is obligated in פאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the custom of the people of יריחו. It cites a משנה that gives the conditions for an obligation of פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires five conditions for an item to be obligated in פאה. The challenge only becomes fully clear in the next step, which explains that one of these conditions excludes vegetables. So why would the people of יריחו give פאה from vegetables?

keyTerms.meaning: Don't they hold (do they not accept)

phrases.english: And don't the people of יריחו hold
that which we learned in a משנה,
They stated a general rule about פאה:
anything that is food, and is guarded,
and grows from the ground, and is harvested all at once,
and is brought in for storage, is obligated in פאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית לְהוּ לְאַנְשֵׁי יְרִיחוֹ הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the custom quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The custom of the people of יריחו to give פאה from vegetables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A standard משנה lists the conditions for פאה, and vegetables do not meet them. So vegetables should be exempt.

steps.title: What each condition excludes, ending with vegetables
steps.stepSummary: Each of the five conditions is explained by what it leaves out. The last condition, storage, excludes vegetables, which makes the challenge sharp.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Anything that is food' excludes the after-growths of woad and safflower. 'Is guarded' excludes ownerless crops. 'Grows from the ground' excludes truffles and mushrooms. 'Harvested all at once' excludes figs. 'Brought in for storage' excludes vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through each condition of the פאה rule and shows what it excludes. This proves that vegetables are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition leaves out a specific item. Dye plants are not food. Ownerless crops are not guarded. Mushrooms do not draw food from the ground. Figs ripen at different times. Vegetables cannot be stored for long. This last point is the core of the challenge: vegetables are exempt from פאה, so why did the people of יריחו give it? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: After-growths of woad and safflower (dye plants)

steps.whatToRemember: Vegetables are excluded from פאה because they are not stored long-term. That is why the custom of the people of יריחו needs an explanation.

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל שֶׁהוּא אוֹכֶל״ — פְּרָט לִסְפִיחֵי סְטִיס וְקוֹצָה.
phrases.english: 'Anything that is food' excludes the after-growths of woad and safflower.
'And is guarded' excludes ownerless crops.
'And grows from the ground' excludes truffles and mushrooms.
'And harvested all at once' excludes figs.
'And brought in for storage' excludes vegetables.
phrases.notes: This is the point that hits the custom of the people of יריחו.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כׇּל שֶׁהוּא אוֹכֶל״ — פְּרָט לִסְפִיחֵי סְטִיס וְקוֹצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה cited in step 16 and shows explicitly that vegetables are excluded.
steps.raayaObject: That vegetables are exempt from פאה, which strengthens the challenge against the people of יריחו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The explanation of the five conditions in the משנה about פאה

steps.title: The case is turnip heads kept by means of something else
steps.stepSummary: רב answers the challenge. The משנה is about turnip heads, which רש״י explains are the turnip leaves, kept by storing them with the bulbs. אנשי יריחו and the חכמים argue whether storing them by means of something else counts as storage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Here we are dealing with turnip heads. They disagree about storing something by means of another substance. One side holds that storing by means of another substance is called storage. The other side holds that it is not called storage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of how אנשי יריחו could give פאה from vegetables, when storage is one of the conditions for פאה. רב says the vegetable in question is turnip heads, which can be stored with help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Per רש״י, the turnip leaves last a long time only when stored together with the bulbs (אימהות); everyone agrees the bulbs themselves keep. אנשי יריחו hold that this kind of assisted storage still counts, so turnips need פאה. The חכמים hold that it does not count, so turnips are exempt. The argument is not about whether the storage rule applies. It is about what counts as storage.

keyTerms.meaning: turnip heads (per רש״י, the turnip leaves)
we are dealing with (the case under discussion)
bringing it in for storage (keeping it to last)
by means of something else (per רש״י, the leaves are kept with the bulbs)

steps.whatToRemember: אנשי יריחו and the חכמים both accept the condition of storage. They only disagree about whether storage that needs help from something else, like the leaves kept with the bulbs, still counts.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אנשי יריחו rejected the list of five conditions. They accept it. They just treat turnip leaves kept with the bulbs as food that is stored.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer removes the sharp challenge from Step 17. It does so by reading the dispute as a question of how to define storage, not as a rejection of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Here we are dealing with turnip heads,
phrases.notes: Turnip heads can last a long time when preserved.

phrases.english: and about bringing it in for storage
by means of another substance, they disagree.
phrases.notes: רש״י: the turnip leaves are stored by means of the bulbs.

phrases.english: One master holds:

phrases.aramaic: מַכְנִיסוֹ לְקִיּוּם עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר —
phrases.english: bringing it in for storage by means of another substance
is called storage,
and the other master holds: it is not called storage.
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים, so turnips need no פאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הָכָא בְּרָאשֵׁי לְפָתוֹת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 16-17 that vegetables are not stored and so should not need פאה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case and redefining the dispute: the case is a vegetable that can be stored with help, and the argument is over the definition of storage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought אנשי יריחו gave פאה from vegetables that are not stored at all, which would go against the משנה of five conditions.
steps.terutzMaskana: They gave פאה only from turnip heads, which they considered stored because they keep by means of something else, the bulbs. The חכמים do not consider that storage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute about whether storage by means of another substance counts as storage for the law of פאה.

steps.title: Long ago people gave פאה from turnips and cabbage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that in earlier times people gave פאה from turnips and cabbage. רבי יוסי adds that they also gave it from leeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: In earlier times, people would give פאה from turnips and cabbage. רבי יוסי says: also from leeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא showing that giving פאה from turnips was once an accepted practice. This fits רב's explanation that the case is turnips.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בראשונה' (in earlier times) tells us that people once treated certain vegetables, especially turnips, as needing פאה. This supports the idea that some held turnips count as stored produce. רבי יוסי widens the list to include leeks.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Originally, they would give פאה
from turnips and cabbage,
Rabbi Yosei says: also from leeks.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ נוֹתְנִין פֵּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that fits רב's claim that the vegetable in question is turnips.
steps.raayaObject: That turnips (and certain other vegetables) were once treated as needing פאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא introduced with תנו רבנן.

steps.title: A second ברייתא lists turnips and leeks
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says people gave פאה from turnips and leeks. רבי שמעון adds that they also gave it from cabbage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: People would give פאה from turnips and leeks. רבי שמעון says: also from cabbage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא with a slightly different list of vegetables that were given פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both ברייתות, turnips are on the list, which matches רב's explanation. The two ברייתות switch which vegetable is the main list and which is the extra view. In the first, leeks are רבי יוסי's addition. In the second, cabbage is רבי שמעון's addition.
steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות agree that turnips were given פאה. They only disagree about cabbage and leeks, and that disagreement is stated in opposite directions in each ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. In the first ברייתא, רבי יוסי adds leeks. In the second, רבי שמעון adds cabbage.

phrases.english: And it was taught in another baraita:
They would give פאה
from turnips and leeks,
Rabbi Shimon says: also from cabbage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: הָיוּ נוֹתְנִין פֵּיאָה לְלֶפֶת וּלְקַפְלוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא with a different list, which the גמרא will next need to reconcile with the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turnips and leeks were given פאה. רבי שמעון holds that cabbage was given פאה as well.
